source_text:
Ταῦτα δὲ καὶ ἕτερα πλείονα λέγων θάρσους καὶ χαρᾶς ἐνεπίμπλατο, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ χάριτος ἐπληροῦτο, ὥστε οὐ μόνον μὴ συμπεσεῖν ταραχθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν λεγομένων πρὸς αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἐκστῆναι, πέμψαι τε τὸν ἑαυτοῦ κήρυκα ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ σταδίου κηρῦξαι τρίς: Πολύκαρπος ὡμολόγησεν ἑαυτὸν Χριστιανὸν εἶναι.
τούτου λεχθέντος ὑπὸ τοῦ κήρυκος, ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων τῶν τὴν Σμύρναν κατοικούντων ἀκατασχέτῳ θυμῷ καὶ μεγάλῃ φωνῇ ἐπεβόα: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τῆς Ἀσίας διδάσκαλος, ὁ πατὴρ τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ὁ τῶν ἡμετέρων θεῶν καθαιρέτης, ὁ πολλοὺς διδάσκων μὴ θύειν μηδὲ προσκυνεῖν. ταῦτα λέγοντες ἐπεβόων καὶ ἠρώτων τὸν Ἀσιάρχην Φίλιππον, ἵνα ἐπαφῇ τῷ Πολυκάρπῳ λέοντα. ὁ δὲ ἔφη, μὴ εἶναι ἐξὸν αὐτῷ, ἐπειδὴ πεπληρώκει τὰ κυνηγέσια.
τότε ἔδοξεν αὐτοῖς ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπιβοῆσαι, ὥστε τὸν Πολύκαρπον ζῶντα κατακαῦσαι. ἔδει γὰρ τὸ τῆς φανερωθείσης αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τοῦ προσκεφαλαίου ὀπτασίας πληρωθῆναι, ὅτε ἰδὼν αὐτὸ καιόμενον προσευχόμενος εἶπεν ἐπιστραφεὶς τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ πιστοῖς προφητικῶς: Δεῖ με ζῶντα καῆναι.
thought_title: The crowd demands Polycarp be burned alive
orientation: Polycarp has just confessed himself a Christian before the proconsul in the stadium, and now the crowd reacts.
pass_a_gloss: And while saying these things and more numerous other things he was filled with courage and joy, and his face was filled with grace, so that not only did he not collapse having been disturbed by the things said to him, but on the contrary the proconsul was astonished, and sent his own herald into the middle of the stadium to proclaim three times: Polycarp has confessed himself to be a Christian. When this was said by the herald, the whole multitude of gentiles and of Jews dwelling in Smyrna with unrestrainable anger and with a great voice shouted: This is the teacher of Asia, the father of the Christians, the destroyer of our gods, the one teaching many not to sacrifice nor to worship. Saying these things they shouted and asked the Asiarch Philip to release a lion against Polycarp. But he said that it was not lawful for him, since he had completed the beast hunts. Then it seemed good to them with one accord to shout that Polycarp be burned alive. For it was necessary that the vision shown to him on the pillow be fulfilled, when seeing it burning he prayed and said turning to the faithful with him prophetically: It is necessary for me to be burned alive.

choices.why: The adjective means not able to be held back; 'unrestrainable' preserves the force of the alpha-privative and the verbal root.
The genitive is possessive/descriptive; 'teacher of Asia' is the most literal rendering.
καθαιρέτης is an agent noun from καθαιρέω, to pull down or destroy; 'destroyer' is the standard literal equivalent.
rejected: the one who tears down our gods

choices.english: to release a lion against Polycarp
choices.why: ἐπαφίημι means to let loose upon; the dative marks the target, so 'against' is needed to convey the hostile direction.
rejected: to set a lion on Polycarp
to send a lion at Polycarp

choices.why: κυνηγέσια refers to the venationes, the wild beast hunts in the arena; 'beast hunts' is the standard technical rendering.
ζῶντα is a predicative participle modifying Polycarp; 'alive' must be explicit to preserve the horror of the demand.

pass_b_english: As Polycarp said these things and more besides, courage and joy filled him, and grace filled his face. He did not collapse in distress at what was being said to him. On the contrary, the proconsul was astonished. The proconsul sent his own herald into the middle of the stadium to proclaim three times: "Polycarp has confessed that he is a Christian."

When the herald said this, the whole crowd of Gentiles and Jews living in Smyrna shouted with unrestrainable anger and a loud voice. They cried out: "This is the teacher of Asia, the father of the Christians, the destroyer of our gods, the one who teaches many not to sacrifice or worship." Shouting these things, they demanded that Philip the provincial official release a lion against Polycarp. But Philip said it was not lawful for him to do so, since he had already completed the beast hunts.

Then it seemed good to them to shout with one accord that Polycarp should be burned alive. For the vision that had been shown to him about his pillow had to be fulfilled. When he saw it burning as he prayed, he turned and said prophetically to the faithful who were with him: "I must be burned alive."

last_rejected.why: Source means 'not be troubled/disturbed and collapse'; 'distress' narrows the sense incorrectly.
last_rejected.ruling: ταραχθέντα is passive aorist participle of ταράσσω, 'troubled/disturbed'; 'distress' captures this well within normal range.

last_rejected.why: Subject is ambiguous; 'He' could be proconsul or Polycarp. Source has proconsul as subject of infinitive.
last_rejected.fix: the proconsul sent his own herald
last_rejected.ruling: Greek πέμψαι τε follows ἐκστῆναι with proconsul as subject; English 'He' correctly refers to proconsul from prior context.

polish.changed: Clarified who is speaking and acting, broke long sentences into natural modern units, and made pronoun references explicit while preserving every claim and quotation.

Clarified that the crowd, not the narrator, speaks the accusations against Polycarp; kept Philip's title consistent as 'provincial official'; smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.

notes.fix: Use 'Asiarch' with a brief note, or 'president of the provincial games.'
